Container & model: M, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`
Clause-②: no — internal cross-request caching bounded by a "cached ≡ uncached" identity pin; no accept/reject change, no public surface widened. ⚠️ If the route requires a new export or changes an observable contract, that is clause ② — stop and report.
Serial constraints cleared: **leg C (#11966) landed** as squash `a8c00e27`, and the **substrate (#11968) landed** as `4bd6faa2` — both on `origin/main` now, so this leg builds on shipped ground rather than an in-flight branch. ⛔ Queued sibling **#12623** (`SchemaRegistry.registerObject` packageId) touches the same registry family and is **serial-queued behind this card** — not dispatched. No open PR touches the registry seam.

### The ruled design — ⛔ not re-adjudicable

Provenance: design = #11633 comment `5394942824` (§4 leg D, §10.2); maintainer acceptance = #11633 comment `5404681591`, 2026-08-25, verbatim, ⛔ untranslated:

> 接受你的建议，继续

with forks **1A / 2B / 3A / TTL-0**. This is **leg D, ship-second** — leg C shipped first and is now on `main`.

**Content**: a cross-request cache for `getMetaItems`' `sys_metadata` read, keyed on the **registry epoch**, reusing the shipped `metadata.changed` channel cross-node.

### ⛔ The hard requirement — this one is a deliverable, not a caveat

> **The SchemaRegistry-hydration trap named in the design (§4 leg D) must be resolved EXPLICITLY in the PR body — stated and designed around, ⛔ not inherited silently.**

Read §4 leg D of the design before writing code and address the trap **in the PR body in your own words**, naming what you measured. ⛔ A PR that implements the cache without that section is incomplete regardless of how green it is.

**Acceptance criterion**: a *"cached answer ≡ uncached answer"* identity pin for `getMetaItems` across an epoch bump (write → epoch change → fresh read), per design §7's pin plan.

### PM mechanism assumptions — ⛔ my readings, confirm or refute

- The card says *"design measured at `992161b728`; re-verify the epoch/channel seams on current `origin/main`"*. ⚠️ `origin/main` has moved a long way since — **including leg C and the substrate landing today**. Re-measure the epoch and `metadata.changed` seams as they actually shipped, ⛔ not as the design predicted they would.
- ⭐ **Leg C is your worked precedent and it is worth reading before you start.** It landed two rules the design did not spell out, both of which may apply here: (1) it caches a success **only when the engine exposes the write-epoch seam**, declining rather than degrading to a TTL-only shape; (2) its invalidation retires **success entries only**, because retiring a failure memo on a write would restart log spam a previous card removed. Whether either transfers to leg D is **yours to measure** — ⛔ do not copy them in, and ⛔ do not assume they do not apply.
- ⚠️ Leg C also **refuted a design prediction**: the design expected an object-scoped backstop on `sys_setting` writes, but the substrate that shipped is **process-wide and object-agnostic** (Fork 1 A), so its backstop over-invalidates — a hit-rate cost, never correctness. Expect the same shape here and say so if you find it.

⛔ Confirm or refute all of the above on the current ref. `premise_still_valid: false` with no PR is a legitimate and valuable delivery.

## ACCEPT — PR #12727

Reviewer of record: `domain:engine` seat, session `session_01LZbWd2jNV1FErXTPSS4Dry` (R2). Verified **against the tree**, ⛔ not against the report.

### Checklist

| Item | Reading |
|---|---|
| Scope | **6 files, +1067 / −23** vs merge base. Matches the report exactly. |
| Fences | ⛔ `packages/spec` **0 changed files** · ⛔ `packages/core/src/security/index.ts` **0** · ⛔ `content/docs/releases/` **0** (four pages read, none edited). All three held. |
| Clause ② | `no`, **verified**: `meta-overlay-cache` appears **0 times** in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` (control: that file carries **36** `export` lines, so the zero is a reading) ⇒ the new module is package-internal. No entry-point export added or removed. |
| CI | ⏳ running on final head `4482c848`, zero red so far. Enqueue gated on every check green. |
| Changeset | `minor`, grade argued in-file. |

### ⭐ The hard requirement is met — and met the right way

The dispatch made the SchemaRegistry-hydration trap a **deliverable**. It is resolved **by placement, not by care**, which is the strongest available form:

> What is cached is the overlay **ROW SET** — the value the two `queryByOrg` calls produce — **never the merged answer**. Every consumer of those rows still runs on every call, hit or miss: overlay parse, package-aware merge, `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry`, MetadataService merge, disabled-package filter, nav contributions, decorations.

⇒ **Hydration cannot be skipped by a hit, so its idempotence never has to be proven — because it is never replayed.** And it is measured, not argued: the test records `registerItem` per call and asserts that after two calls the engine was read **once** while the registry hydrated **twice**, same rows same order; a third call makes it three. Ablation 2 shows it from the other side.

⭐ **The larger sibling this placement also closes is the best single observation in this round:** `getMetaItems`' answer depends on **four** mutable sources (`sys_metadata` rows, SchemaRegistry, MetadataService, artifact table), and the epoch observes **only the first**. Caching the *merged* answer would have served three sources that **nothing in the key can validate**.

> Keeping the cache's reach co-extensive with what its key validates is the load-bearing property.

That is a rule worth more than this card, and I want it quotable.

### ⚠️ A design claim refuted, and it changed the implementation

The card says leg D *"reuses the shipped `metadata.changed` channel cross-node."* **Measured false, and the dev did not build on it:**

- `metadata.changed` is published by `MetadataManager.notifyWatchers`;
- the writer whose rows this cache holds is `SysMetadataRepository`;
- `protocol.ts` contains **zero** `notifyWatchers` / `subscribe` / `watchService` calls.

⇒ The dev **did not subscribe**. Cross-node for leg D is `authz.invalidated` plus the TTL. ✅ Refuting a card's own content sentence rather than implementing around it is exactly what `premise_still_valid` is for — and this refutation is also what put the one docs page in scope.

### Leg C's two rules — measured for transfer, ⛔ neither copied nor assumed

I asked explicitly not to copy them in and not to assume they don't apply. Both were measured:

- **Rule 1 (no seam, no cache) TRANSFERS** — pinned, including that a partial `{ current }` is not a seam. ✅
- **Rule 2 (retire successes only) does NOT transfer** — and this is reported as a **measured finding, not an omission**: leg D has **no failure memo to protect**, and nothing is cached when the read throws. ✅ That distinction is the difference between a considered decision and a gap.

### Two corrections the dev made rather than absorbed

- **`check:engine-double-contract` went red once**, and its own verdict line prescribed the remedy: *"Run `--write` and commit"* — i.e. **widen the ledger**. ⛔ The dev **did not take it**: no case calls `findOne` (the overlay path issues exactly one verb, `find`), so it **deleted the unexercised double** instead. **Ledger untouched**, gate green on re-run, 20/20 still pass. ⭐ Refusing a gate's own offer to widen a ratchet, because the honest fix was smaller, is the right instinct and the rarer one.
- **Deep-cloned cached rows in both directions**, correctness-critical: the downstream merge **mutates `record.metadata`** when it is an object. Rows that will not clone are not cached. That is a real hazard a naive cache would have shipped.

### Ablations — predictions committed to git *before* each mutation
